messages:
mira: Heads-up — filing an RBAC change request for the BYOK controller we're onboarding for acme-corp. Need quick alignment on who can request 'export-wrapped-key' tokens and what audit stream we must persist for compliance. Ticket: https://redwood/issue/INF-4821 :eyes:

ken: scope? is this just the controller role or all operator roles (deploy, oncall, keystore-admin)?

mira: primarily controller and keystore-admin. deploy/oncall should only see meta-events (request id, status) not the wrapped key op. Legal asked for separation between 'requester' and 'approver' in the flow.

liam: propose a new minimal role 'key-approver' that can sign export requests but cannot read key metadata. Implementation sketch (IAM policy):

```
{
  "Action": ["kms:SignExportRequest", "kms:ReadApprovalQueue"],
  "Resource": ["arn:redwood:kms:*/customer/*/byok-controller"],
  "Effect": "Allow"
}
```

liam: that keeps export approval auditable and separates it from keystore-admin which handles lifecycle ops. :lock:

tara: compliance note — for EU financial customers we need immutable audit logs retained for 7 years and export requests must contain the approver id + rationale. Also need an SLA on delivery of audit evidence for audits (72h).

mira: thanks. on the audit pipeline, do we stream full event payloads to the external audit bucket (S3/GCS) or do we only stream redacted events and keep full payloads in internal secure archive?

sre_jose: operational constraints: streaming full wrapped-key blobs out is a no-go. We should stream structured events (request_id, action, outcome, approver, timestamp, region, controller_version) and keep wrapped artifacts in our HSM-backed secure vault with access only via signed ephemeral jobs. Example log line from staging: `audit-service: event=key_export request_id=aa12 outcome=denied actor=keystore-admin`.

mira: so auditstream = structured events to external bucket, full wrapped key artifacts remain in private keystore. Agreed?

ken: agreed, but we need a consistent correlation id so auditors can map structured events -> stored artifact references. Add `artifact_handle` (opaque id) to events, not the blob itself.

liam: also add hash and HSM-slot-id to the event so offline verification is possible: `artifact_hash=sha256:...`, `slot=HSM-03`. That satisfies integrity checks without leaking key material.

tara: legal OK with artifact_handle + hash + approver metadata + retention policy. Please make sure export rationale field is free-text and stored in the immutable audit stream.

mira: vuln triage question — we recently saw a dependency vuln in the keystore agent (CVE-2025-xxxx) that allows local privilege escalation. If an operator with keystore-admin role is compromised, does our separation prevent key export?

liam: with the proposed 'key-approver' role separated and export requiring an approver signature, compromise of a single keystore-admin should not allow export. But if agent is exploited to forge approval calls, we need strong mTLS and signer keys in HSM to validate approver signatures.

sre_jose: also add detection rules: alert if `export` request_count per user > threshold within X minutes, or if approvals come from an unusual region/IP. sec-bot kicked off a rule scan and found no existing rule.

sec-bot: Alert rule suggestion created: `escalate_on_unusual_approver_activity` — file: /rules/approver_abuse.yml. (auto-note) :robot_face:

mira: incident response plan draft: if suspicious export attempt detected -> 1) block further export ops globally (automated fallback) 2) page sec-oncall + keystore-admin pager 3) snapshot auditstream and HSM event logs 4) rotate ephemeral signer certs if compromise confirmed. We need playbook steps for each.

ken: for step 1, we can use a policy flag in the controller feature-flags service `disallow_external_exports=true` to immediately reject new exports at the edge. Good to have a kill-switch.

liam: note: kill-switch must be replicated to all regions and validated by health checks, otherwise partial enforcement causes confusing audit gaps. Add a canary that verifies flag propagation before we rely on it.

mira: action items: 1) liam to draft IAM role and controller changes (PR) 2) liam + sre_jose to add artifact_handle/hash fields to audit schema 3) tara to confirm retention+witness wording for contracts 4) ken to add kill-switch runbook and canary 5) sec-eng to author incident playbook. I'll open PRs and link here.

mira: PRs: https://redwood/pull/4728 (RBAC + approval flow), https://redwood/pull/4729 (audit schema + rules). Will tag sec-oncall and legal reviewers.

sre_jose: quick test snippet for generating artifact handle (for reviewers):
```
handle=$(uuidgen)-$(date +%s)
hash=$(sha256sum artifact.bin | awk '{print $1}')
echo "artifact_handle=$handle artifact_hash=sha256:$hash"
```

mira: perfect. I'll update the ticket and request a tabletop with sec-oncall + SRE tomorrow at 10am. Thanks all :raised_hands:

liam: looks good. I'll start the PR and add unit tests for schema validation.

tara: I'll send the retention wording and SLA clause to the contract repo; ping me if auditors ask for sample evidence.

ken: adding kill-switch docs now.

sec-bot: Reminder — please add automated tests to prevent regressions for `key-approver` role. (auto-reminder)

mira: noted. closing loop here, will follow up in PR threads.
